proof_scope: The only runtime read of the Quick Claw roll affecting behavior is guarded by current held Quick Claw in get_pokemon_action_speed. All callers use that function; the remaining reads serialize/hash or diagnose the state.

Runtime held-item writes remove items or transfer an existing item through Thief. The guard scans both complete rosters, including benched and fainted holders, so absence is forward invariant. Existing cached speeds and all other state fields remain hashed.

The key has separate tags for exact, no damage history, no Quick Claw roll, and both quotients. The public engine key rejects dropping observable fields. Ordinary engine/search keys preserve their field hashes.

Tests cover both quotient-key modes, Counter retaining damage history, active/bench/fainted holders, complete stochastic successor kernels with switching and Thief, and two-turn exhaustive value enclosure. A held-item negative control changes win payoff from 0.5 to 1.0 when the roll changes and keeps distinct keys.
conclusions: At approximately 120000 nodes, the same-binary root control upper bound is 0.0230607590 after 1127872 executions and the quotient upper bound is 0.0206433156 after 1113516 executions. Wall times came from differently overlapped runs and are not a speed benchmark.

The dedicated 1v1 result worsens from upper 0.1486582361 at 521348 executions to 0.1528024165 at 1103466 executions, both stopping near 120000 nodes. Exact merging changes refinement order and is not universally beneficial at finite budget. Keep the option off by default.

The extended quotient root stops at its 180-second limit with 1938796 executions and 192655 nodes. Its side-one strategy guarantees 0.9864396882. Both archived first-decision loss upper bounds fall from 0.0201189219 to 0.0135603121, including outward numerical padding, and now meet the 0.02 tolerance.

Rebuilt default values, full root matrices, node counts and stop reason reproduce the previous dedicated 1v1 record exactly. Engine execution counts do not: 971342 becomes 521348, and the pure forced-replacement enumeration changes from 3 executions to 2. The current enumerator reuses its initial scripted result, matching the 2-run census; older manifests lack engine-source hashes, so a stale prior dependency is an inference, not established provenance. All new comparison arms have the same binary hash; archived work counts are not used for speed claims.

No positive archived first-decision loss lower bound, deployed bot strength improvement, or global optimality is established. This state now has a full-information near-optimal first-decision certificate and can leave the 0.02 unresolved queue.
